FARRA:v3p203/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p203/r1.speaker: أبي
FARRA:v3p203/r1.claim: Ubayy's reading has the nominative singular nadhīrun lil-bashar, “a warner to humankind”; both readings are sound.

FARRA:v3p204/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p204/r7.speaker: بعض النحويين
FARRA:v3p204/r7.claim: Some grammarians connect accusative nadhīran to the opening command, “rise as a warner to humankind.”

FARRA:v3p204/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p204/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p204/r8.claim: Al-Farrāʾ rejects that distant connection because much speech intervenes and Ubayy's nominative reading rules it out.

FARRA:v3p204/r9.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p204/r9.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p204/r9.claim: He instead connects nadhīran with “one of the great calamities,” treating it as an indefinite accusative separated from a definite noun, or as a verbal noun of warning.

TAB-FULL:v23p445/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī first glosses “a warning to humankind” as Hell warning human beings; on this reading nadhīran is an accusative detached modifier of “one of the greatest.”

TAB-FULL:v23p445/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r2.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says people were warned of no greater or more dreadful calamity than this.

TAB-FULL:v23p445/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r3.speaker: أبو رزين
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r3.claim: Abū Razīn takes God as the subject: God says He warns people of Hell so they should fear it.

TAB-FULL:v23p445/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r4.claim: Another grammatical interpretation makes nadhīran an accusative verbal noun, “a warning,” outside the prior clause, or says the Fire was made one of the great matters as a warning.

TAB-FULL:v23p445/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v23p445/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says “humankind” means the children of Adam and identifies Muhammad as the warner, with nadhīran construed as a circumstantial accusative after “arise.”

ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r5.claim: Nadhīran may instead be masculine by analogy with a woman called ṭāhir or ṭāliq, meaning one possessing purity or divorce, hence “possessing warning.”

ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p248#2/r6.claim: Alternatively, nadhīran can attach to the opening of the sūra: “arise as a warner to humankind.”

NAHHAS:v5p72/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p72/r1.speaker: الحسن
NAHHAS:v5p72/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan says no warning is more terrifying than Hell, or words to that effect.

NAHHAS:v5p72/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p72/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
NAHHAS:v5p72/r2.claim: Abū Razīn says God Himself is a warner to mankind.

NAHHAS:v5p72/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p72/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
NAHHAS:v5p72/r3.claim: Ibn Zayd says Muhammad is the warner to mankind.

NAHHAS:v5p72/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p72/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p72/r4.claim: Abu Jaʿfar records seven parses of nadhīran: circumstantial from anā or ihdā al-kubar, from a Fire-as-warning reading, implied clauses for God's warning, an imperative for Muhammad, verbal noun indhār, or 'I mean a warner.'

NAHHAS:v5p72/r5.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p72/r5.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p72/r5.claim: If nadhīr describes the Fire, its yāʾ is omitted as a relational adjective.

SULAMI:v2p359#5/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p359#5/r2.speaker: الواسطي
SULAMI:v2p359#5/r2.claim: When lights appear to the spirits of the unifiers, prophetic warning returns those absorbed in conformity to their witness; at direct vision, conformity itself has no significance.

THALABI:v10p76/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p76/r1.speaker: الخليل
THALABI:v10p76/r1.claim: Al-Khalil says nadhir is a verbal noun like nakir, which allows it to describe a feminine subject; another construction makes it God's warning to humanity.

THALABI:v10p76/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p76/r2.speaker: أبو رزين
THALABI:v10p76/r2.claim: Abu Razin explains the warning as the speaker saying he warns people about the Fire and urges them to avoid it.

THALABI:v10p76/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p76/r3.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v10p76/r3.claim: Another interpretation makes the warning a description of Muhammad, meaning he is commanded to rise and warn humanity.

THALABI:v10p76/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p76/r4.speaker: إبراهيم عن أبي غيلة
THALABI:v10p76/r4.claim: Ibrahim transmits a nominative reading nadhirun li-l-bashar, with an implicit huwa.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r1.claim: The warning to humanity is Muhammad, commanded to rise and warn.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r2.speaker: الحسن
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r2.claim: The warning to humanity may be the Fire, the most dreadful thing ever used to warn creation.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p147/r3.claim: It may also be the Qur'an, with its promises and threats.

QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r15.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r15.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p364/r15.claim: The warning to humankind cautions against worldly distractions that interrupt access to reality and against settling into pride over acts of obedience, which have no independent weight.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r1.claim: Nadhiran means an imperative: rise as a warner to mankind; al-Kisaʾi and al-Zajjaj cite this as an accusative parsing.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r2.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r2.claim: He rejects the imperative explanation because much intervenes; nadhiran is an accusative detached from the definite phrase ihda al-kubar.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r3.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r3.claim: Alternatively, nadhir can mean warning, so the phrase means warn mankind with a warning; the description of Hell supports this.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r4.claim: He treats nadhiran as a circumstantial expression, masculine in form because it describes punishment or means possessing a warning, like a woman described as pure or divorced.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r5.claim: He gives two possible circumstantial antecedents: the command to rise near the beginning of the surah, or the phrase one of the great calamities.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r6.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v22p448/r6.claim: On either parse, he takes nadhiran as a verbal noun used circumstantially, which can modify a feminine singular or feminine plural, as well as a singular.

JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r7.claim: The common reading has naḏīran in the accusative, understood as a command to the wrapped Prophet to rise as a warner, or as a circumstantial expression attached to the preceding verse.

JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r8.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r8.claim: Abu Muslim also parses naḏīran as an accusative of specification.

JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r9.speaker: إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة
JISHUMI:v10p7165#2/r9.claim: Ibrahim ibn Abi Abla reads naḏīr in the nominative, meaning that it is a warner.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r3.speaker: الحسن
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r3.claim: Al-Hasan says no warning from God is more dreadful than the fire; نذيرا is an accusative specification after the definite ‘one of the great.’

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r4.speaker: الخليل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r4.claim: Al-Khalil calls نذير a verbal noun like نكير, allowing it to describe a feminine referent.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r5.speaker: أبو رزين
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r5.claim: Another interpretation makes the warning a description of God’s act: ‘I warn you of it, so beware.’

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p272#2/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd takes it as Muhammad’s role: ‘O you wrapped up, arise as a warner to humanity.’

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd says Muhammad is the Warner; Khalil prefers this construction, which also allows نذيرا to describe a feminine noun.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r11.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r11.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads نذير in the nominative, with an implicit هو.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r8.speaker: الحسن
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r8.claim: Hasan says the warning itself is from the Fire; نذيرا can be circumstantial to the pronoun in إنها or to لإحدى.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r9.speaker: أبو رزين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p397#2/r9.claim: Abu Razin says God is the Warner, requiring an implied governing verb such as appoint or summon.

TABRISI:74:36-37/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:36-37/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:36-37/r1.claim: ‘A warner to humankind’ may be a circumstantial participle describing Hell as one of the great calamities, with the feminine referent understood as possessing warning; the masculine form can mean ‘possessing warning.’

TABRISI:74:36-37/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:36-37/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:36-37/r12.claim: A warner is a wise guide who alerts people to what they should fear; every prophet warns of God's punishment for disobedience.

TABRISI:74:36-37/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:36-37/r14.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:74:36-37/r14.claim: Alternatively, the warner is the Prophet, as in the command at the start of the sura to rise and warn.

TABRISI:74:36-37/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:36-37/r15.speaker: ابن رزين
TABRISI:74:36-37/r15.claim: Another view takes the warner as God, with the phrase circumstantial to the omitted oath verb.

TABRISI:74:36-37/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:36-37/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:36-37/r2.claim: Alternatively, the phrase attaches to the opening address: ‘O enwrapped one, rise as a warner to humankind.’

TABRISI:74:36-37/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:74:36-37/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:74:36-37/r3.claim: A third analysis reads nadhīr as a verbal noun, ‘warning,’ in the accusative as an object-like cognate accusative.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p410#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p410#3/r1.speaker: الزجاج
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p410#3/r1.claim: Naḏīran is an accusative circumstantial expression: Saqar is among the greatest calamities in its role as a warning to humanity; it may also attach to the opening command, rise as a warner.

RAZI-FULL:v30p184#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v30p184#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v30p184#3/r1.claim: Nadhīran may be an accusative specification explaining that Saqar is one of the great calamities as a warning, or a circumstantial accusative; Ubayy reads the nominative as a predicate or with an omitted subject.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r10.claim: Another view makes the Quran itself the warning because it contains promises and threats.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r2.speaker: الزجاج
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r2.claim: Al-Zajjaj says nadhiran means the Fire is a warning to humanity, functioning as a circumstantial accusative; masculine form reflects its meaning as punishment or as “possessing warning.”

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r3.speaker: الخليل
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r3.claim: Al-Khalil treats nadhir as a verbal noun like nakir, which explains its use for a feminine referent.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r4.speaker: الحسن
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r4.claim: Hasan says creation has never been warned of anything more terrifying than the Fire.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r5.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي وابن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r5.claim: They interpret the warner as Muhammad, resuming the command at the start of the sura to rise and warn; this is also reported from Ibn Abbas.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r6.speaker: الفراء
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r6.claim: Al-Farra rejects attaching nadhiran to the opening command because too much text intervenes; another report says this syntax is awkward for the same reason.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r7.speaker: أبو رزين
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r7.claim: Abu Razin says God Himself is the warner, telling people to fear the Fire.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r8.claim: Other syntactic proposals make nadhiran a circumstantial phrase referring to the one who knows God’s forces, or a verbal noun meaning warning; it may also modify an implied verb.

QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r9.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
QURTUBI-FULL:74:35-37/r9.claim: Ibn Abi Abla reads nadhir in the nominative, supplying an implied “it is.”

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:32-38/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:32-38/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:32-38/r6.claim: نذيرا للبشر may be an accusative specification (‘a warning’), a state inferred from the clause, or nominative as a second predicate or predicate of an omitted subject.

BAYDAWI-FULL:74:32-38/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:32-38/r7.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:74:32-38/r7.claim: The warning is for people able to advance toward good or lag behind; another parsing connects لمن شاء to أن يتقدم, echoing the choice formula in 18:29.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p297#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p297#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p297#5/r1.claim: Nadhīran is a specification of “one of the great calamities,” meaning a warning, and “for humankind” is an appositive.

QASHANI:74:36/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:36/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:36/r1.claim: The denial that this is a warning for everyone reflects that most people are unprepared, their hearts sealed and fated for misery, so they do not heed it.

QASHANI:74:36/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:74:36/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:74:36/r3.claim: The hell of nature is a great calamity and warning, but it warns only receptive people who may gain virtues and approach heart and spirit, while others descend into bodily desire.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r1.speaker: الجمهور
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r1.claim: Nadhiran may be a verbal noun meaning warning, used as a specification: one of the greatest calamities as a warning.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r2.speaker: الفراء
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r2.claim: Al-Farraʾ treats nadhiran as a verbal noun governed by an omitted verb: ‘warn as a warning.’

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads nadhiran as an active participle in the circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in innaha.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r4.claim: The proposed attachments to the opening command, its later warning command, or al-kubar and its pronoun are unsound; Abu al-Baqaʾ’s circumstantial reading from the whole clause’s implied sense is acceptable.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r5.speaker: النحاس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r5.claim: Al-Nahhas explains the missing feminine ending in nadhiran as a relational form meaning ‘possessing warning,’ referring to the fire.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r6.speaker: علي بن سليمان والحسن وابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r6.claim: Ali b. Sulayman takes nadhiran as ‘I mean a warner’; al-Hasan reads it as ‘that I may warn,’ and Ibn ʿAtiyya says this makes it circumstantial from innaha or li-ihda.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r7.speaker: أبو رزين وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r7.claim: Abu Razin identifies the warner as God with an omitted verb; Ibn Zayd identifies him as Muhammad, likewise supplied by an omitted verb.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r8.speaker: أبي وابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p336/r8.claim: They read nadhir in the nominative; it can predicate an omitted ‘it is’ for the fire or an omitted ‘he is’ for God or the Messenger.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r1.claim: One analysis makes ‘nadhiran’ an accusative specification of ‘ihda’, which conveys greatness; it means warning just as nakir means denunciation, as in the example ‘one of the women in chastity’.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r10.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة، أبي بن كعب
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r10.claim: The common reading has ‘nadhiran’ in the accusative; Ibn Abi ‘Abla and Ubayy ibn Ka‘b read it nominative. If Hell is intended it can be a second predicate or predicate of omitted ‘hiya’; if God or the Messenger is intended, an omitted ‘huwa’ is understood.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r11.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r11.claim: ‘Lil-bashar’ may be an adjective or the object of ‘nadhir’; the preposition li- is extra, strengthening the governor.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r2.speaker: الفراء
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r2.claim: Al-Farra’ treats ‘nadhiran’ as a verbal noun meaning warning, governed by an omitted verb.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r3.speaker: الزجاج
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes ‘nadhir’ as an active form with a passive sense and a circumstantial accusative from the pronoun in ‘innaha’.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r4.claim: Other proposed governors make it circumstantial from ‘ihda’ understood as magnificent, from the subject of ‘qum’ at the sura’s opening, or a verbal noun governed by ‘anذir’ there.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r5.claim: Further analyses make it circumstantial from ‘al-kubar’ or its pronoun, from ‘li-ihda’ per Ibn ‘Atiyya, or an accusative with an omitted ‘I mean’.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r6.claim: It may instead be governed by an omitted ‘call’ with God intended, or by ‘call’ or ‘convey’ with the Messenger intended; another analysis supplies ‘it became a warning’.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r7.claim: Additional circumstantial analyses attach it to the pronoun in ‘kubar’ or ‘huwa’ in the statement that none knows the Lord’s hosts but Him.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r8.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r8.claim: Abu al-Baqa treats it as an object of purpose, governed by the verbal meaning in ‘al-kubar’; the author calls that analysis distant.

SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r9.speaker: أبو جعفر
SAMIN-DURR:74:36/r9.claim: When ‘nadhiran’ is circumstantial from a feminine noun, its masculine form is explained by an implied ‘possessing warning’ and a relational sense, according to Abu Ja‘far.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p233/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p233/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p233/r6.claim: Nadhir may describe a tremendous warner, the warning conveyed by the fire, or a warning of exceptional force; nadhir can function as an intensive or a verbal noun.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p234/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p234/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p234/r1.claim: Calling the warning one for all humanity fits how quickly bodily beings are affected, especially by fire.

DURR-FULL:v8p335/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p335/r3.speaker: حذيفة
DURR-FULL:v8p335/r3.claim: Hudhayfa says a caller warns each morning and evening that people must depart; he links this warning to the Quran's call to advance or fall behind.

BURSEVI:v10p184/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p184/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p184/r4.claim: Nadhiran is an accusative of specification: Sakar is among the greatest terrors as a warning; its masculine form is explained by construing the pronoun as punishment or as “possessing warning.”

ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhshari takes نذيرا as a verbal noun meaning warning and a specification of إحدى الكبر: Saqar is a great calamity as a warning.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r2.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r2.claim: Al-Farra treats نذيرا as a verbal noun governed by an implied verb.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r3.speaker: الزجاج
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj reads it as an active participle meaning warning and as a circumstantial phrase linked to the pronoun in إنها.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r4.claim: Abu al-Baqa makes it a circumstantial phrase for what the clause implies, with an estimated sense of becoming great or immense.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r5.speaker: النحاس
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r5.claim: Al-Nahhas explains the missing feminine marker as an attribution meaning ذات إنذار, as in the idiom رحمة الله قريب.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r6.speaker: أبو رزين
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r6.claim: Abu Razin takes the warner to be God, with an implied command such as ادع.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the warner to be the Prophet with an implied verb such as proclaim; the author calls this strained and an innovative interpretation.

ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r8.speaker: أبي وابن أبي عبلة
ALUSI-FULL:v29p131/r8.claim: Ubayy and Ibn Abi ʿAbla read نذير in the nominative as a second predicate of إن or as the predicate of an omitted subject.

ELMALILI:74:32-56/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:74:32-56/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:74:32-56/r3.claim: The phrase may mean that seqar warns humanity, or that it is a warning as to humanity; some attach it to the sura’s opening command to stand as a warner.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p320/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p320/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p320/r4.claim: Alternatively, كلا rejects in advance the following claim that the passage is a warning to humanity, since people should heed it but most do not; this favors joining it in recitation.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p322/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p322/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v29p322/r6.claim: نذيرا is circumstantial from the pronoun in إنها: Saqar is among the greatest calamities while warning humanity, and that alone suffices as a warning.

TABATABAI:74:35-38/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:35-38/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:35-38/r1.claim: The passage clears the Quran of the accusation against it: it is one of God's greatest signs and warns all humanity, freeing those who follow it from deeds that bind them to Saqar.

TABATABAI:74:35-38/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:35-38/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:74:35-38/r8.claim: Nadhiran is an accusative verbal noun meaning warning; another view takes it as a circumstantial modifier meaning that the sign is majestic while warning.

TABATABAI:74:35-38/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:74:35-38/r9.speaker: بعضهم
TABATABAI:74:35-38/r9.claim: The author dismisses other readings that make nadhiran an adjective for the Prophet or God.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p32/r4.claim: Nature’s manifestations argue for the Hereafter and expose heedlessness; the Qur’an warns so people can prepare, while evaders are left with stubbornness as their excuse.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p55/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p55/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p55/r1.claim: The Qur'anic warning verses complete the preceding oaths: their account of Hell describes a great upheaval, not a jest, so mockers are unfortunate.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:32/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:32/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:32/r1.claim: The oaths by the moon, departing night, and dawning morning draw attention both to divine signs and to the importance of the warning to humanity.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:32/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:32/r2.speaker: farklı görüşler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:74:32/r2.claim: The thing described as a warning to humanity has been identified variously as hell, the Quran, or the Prophet.

STUDYQURAN:74:36/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:36/r1.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:74:36/r1.claim: Some exegetes attach verse 36 grammatically to the command in verses 1–2: the Prophet is to rise and warn humanity.

STUDYQURAN:74:36/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:36/r2.speaker: Q, Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:74:36/r2.claim: Most relate it to verse 35, so Saqar’s gravity itself serves as a warning.

STUDYQURAN:74:36/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:74:36/r3.speaker: Q
STUDYQURAN:74:36/r3.claim: In context, “warner” may be an Attribute of God or refer to the Quran.
